codebase_summary:
PROJECT OVERVIEW:
CodeGuard is a GitHub-integrated AI agent built on the Claude Agent SDK that automatically reviews pull requests for security vulnerabilities and code quality issues, posts structured review comments back to GitHub, and generates onboarding documentation (CONTRIBUTING.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, SETUP.md) for new repositories upon their first push.

LANGUAGE AND STACK:
Python 3.11 is the sole programming language. The project uses the Claude Agent SDK as its AI orchestration layer, calling Anthropic models (claude-sonnet-4-6 for deep analysis and claude-haiku-4-5 for simpler summarization tasks) via an async streaming interface. PyGithub wraps the GitHub REST API for reading pull request diffs and committing files. python-dotenv loads environment variables from a .env file. PyYAML parses the .codeguard.yml configuration file. The standard library modules asyncio, json, hashlib, os, datetime, and zoneinfo are used throughout. No web framework is present since the project is designed to run as a GitHub Actions job rather than a long-running server.

ENTRY POINTS:
src/main.py is the sole entry point. It is invoked directly by the GitHub Actions workflow runner via the command python src/main.py. On startup it reads the EVENT_NAME environment variable to determine which pipeline to execute: a pull request review pipeline, a push-triggered onboarding pipeline, or a manual onboarding triggered by an issue comment containing the string "/onboard".

DIRECTORY STRUCTURE:
src/ contains every Python source module that implements the two agent pipelines (PR review and onboarding). docs/ holds the phased project planning documents (plan.md, phase1.md, phase2.md, phase3.md, template.md) which describe the design rationale and implementation roadmap. venv/ is the local Python virtual environment directory, excluded from version control. The repository root contains configuration files, documentation outputs, and the generated session log.

KEY MODULES:
src/main.py is the orchestrator and entry point; it reads environment variables, loads configuration, branches on event type, and calls into the appropriate pipeline functions.
src/github_client.py wraps PyGithub to provide four utility functions: fetching a PR diff, listing changed files, posting a PR comment with retry logic, and creating or updating a file in the repository.
src/gather_context.py assembles a plain-text context block from the PR number, repository name, changed file list, and raw diff; this block is passed as input to each review agent.
src/security_scan.py invokes the Claude Agent SDK with a focused security-analysis prompt scoped to the Read tool; it returns a structured FINDINGS block filtered by the configured severity threshold.
src/quality_review.py invokes the Claude Agent SDK with a code quality prompt scoped to the Read tool; it returns a structured QUALITY NOTES block.
src/summarize_pr.py invokes claude-haiku-4-5 to produce a concise plain-English SUMMARY of the pull request intent, affected areas, and trade-offs.
src/post_results.py composes the three review outputs into a single markdown comment body and posts it to the PR via github_client.
src/detect_new_repo.py checks whether CONTRIBUTING.md exists in the target repository root; its absence signals that onboarding is needed.
src/explore_codebase.py runs the Claude Agent SDK with Glob, Read, and Bash tools to map the repository structure and produce a comprehensive codebase summary; it reads from and writes to the local cache before and after the exploration.
src/gen_contributing.py feeds the codebase summary into a prompt that produces a raw CONTRIBUTING.md document.
src/gen_architecture.py feeds the codebase summary into a prompt that produces a raw ARCHITECTURE.md document.
src/gen_setup_guide.py feeds the codebase summary into a prompt that produces a raw SETUP.md document.
src/cache.py manages a JSON file (.codeguard_cache.json) that stores an MD5 hash of the repository file tree and the most recent codebase summary, preventing redundant AI exploration calls on unchanged repositories.
src/config.py reads .codeguard.yml using PyYAML and merges it with hardcoded defaults for the security, quality, summary, and onboarding feature flags.
src/logger.py defines SessionLogger, which records each agent invocation's name, prompt length, result length, a 300-character result preview, and a timestamp; the accumulated log is saved to codeguard_session.json at the end of each run.

DEPENDENCIES:
claude-agent-sdk provides the async query interface and ClaudeAgentOptions class used to dispatch all AI agent calls to Anthropic models with scoped tool permissions.
pygithub is the Python wrapper around the GitHub REST API used to fetch PR diffs, list changed files, post comments, and commit documentation files.
python-dotenv reads the .env file at startup to populate environment variables such as ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, GITHUB_TOKEN, REPO_NAME, EVENT_NAME, PR_NUMBER, and COMMENT_BODY.
pyyaml parses the .codeguard.yml configuration file into a Python dictionary.
tzdata supplies the IANA timezone database required by the standard library zoneinfo module on Windows, enabling the SessionLogger to record timestamps in the America/Los_Angeles timezone.

CONFIG FILES:
.codeguard.yml is the primary user-facing configuration file; it controls whether each of the four feature modules (security, quality, summary, onboarding) is enabled, and sets the security severity threshold to low, medium, or high.
.env stores all runtime secrets and environment variables including ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, GITHUB_TOKEN, REPO_NAME, EVENT_NAME, PR_NUMBER, and COMMENT_BODY; it is excluded from version control via .gitignore.
.gitignore excludes venv/, .env, all __pycache__ directories, compiled .pyc files, and .codeguard_cache.json.
.codeguard_cache.json is a generated runtime file that persists the repository structure hash and cached codebase summary between runs; it is excluded from version control.
codeguard_session.json is a generated runtime file written at the end of each agent session containing a timestamped log of every agent invocation.
requirements.txt declares the five direct Python dependencies: claude-agent-sdk, pygithub, python-dotenv, pyyaml, and tzdata.
venv/pyvenv.cfg records the Python interpreter version and path used to create the local virtual environment.
